Bill.BriefDescription: Regarding recognition of common course numbering at institutions of higher education.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to recognition of lower division courses atinstitutions of higher education; and adding a new section to chapter28B.10 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 28B.10 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The higher education coordinating board and the state board forcommunity and technical colleges shall convene a work group includingrepresentatives from each of the institutions of higher education toestablish a single set of common course numbers and common coursedescriptions for all common lower division courses at all institutionsof higher education. Lower division courses are those first and secondyear courses numbered between ninetynine and three hundred, includinginternships, cooperative learning, field experiences, individualresearch, special seminars, and independent studies. (2) A course shall be identified as common between institutions ofhigher education if the course descriptions in the official collegecourse catalogs are similar enough to be accepted as equivalent for p. 1 HB 1525transfer purposes to meet degree requirements. Once identified ascommon, a course must have the same course number and be accepted asequivalent at each institution. (3) By August 2013, each institution of higher education shallformally adopt the common course numbers and specifically identify themin all course catalogs and publications. Unique courses with noequivalent at another institution or at some but not all institutionsmust have common course numbers at all institutions that do haveequivalent courses and the limitations shall be noted in all coursecatalogs and publications.
